experiments.name: Programmed freezing of Tris-egg-yolk-glycerol bull semen in 0.5 mL straws (5 to -140 °C at 5/40/20 °C/min, Mini Digitcool UJ400) with plunge into liquid nitrogen
experiments.plain_name: Freeze bull semen straws for artificial insemination in a programmable freezer
experiments.description: USDA ARS National Animal Germplasm Program protocol: bull semen extended in Tris-egg yolk (final 7% glycerol) is cooled to 5 °C over 2 h, loaded into 0.5 mL straws and frozen in a programmable freezer on a three-segment curve (5 to -10 °C at 5 °C/min, -10 to -110 °C at 40 °C/min, -110 to -140 °C at 20 °C/min), then plunged into liquid nitrogen for storage and later thawed 30 s at 37 °C for artificial insemination of cattle.

requirements.rationale: The freezing curve starts at 5 °C (278.15 K) and ends at -140 °C (133.15 K) inside the freezer chamber before the plunge, so the chamber must control temperature across that whole span.
requirements.document_title: USDA ARS National Animal Germplasm Program: Bull Semen Collection, Transportation, Processing and Cryopreservation Protocol (P. Purdy; created May 2015, modified April 2020)
requirements.quote: Programmable freezer: The samples are frozen using the Cryo Bio System Mini Digitcool UJ400 (IMV Corporation, Minneapolis, MN) with the following curve: 5 °C to -10 °C at 5 °C/min; -10 °C to -110°C at 40 °C/min; -110°C to -140°C at 20°C/min and then plunged into liquid nitrogen for storage.

requirements.rationale: The curve uses controlled cooling rates of 5, 40 and 20 °C/min, so the freezer must impose rates from 5 °C/min (5000 mK/min) to 40 °C/min (40000 mK/min).
requirements.document_title: USDA ARS National Animal Germplasm Program: Bull Semen Collection, Transportation, Processing and Cryopreservation Protocol (P. Purdy; created May 2015, modified April 2020)
requirements.quote: Programmable freezer: The samples are frozen using the Cryo Bio System Mini Digitcool UJ400 (IMV Corporation, Minneapolis, MN) with the following curve: 5 °C to -10 °C at 5 °C/min; -10 °C to -110°C at 40 °C/min; -110°C to -140°C at 20°C/min and then plunged into liquid nitrogen for storage.

requirements.rationale: At -140 °C the straws are plunged into liquid nitrogen for storage; liquid nitrogen must be available at the freezer.

requirements.rationale: The method is a programmed, controlled-rate freeze; the core temperature and rate keys already decide most machines, so this documented-process flag is supporting only.

experiments.plain_name: Freeze bull semen straws on a rack held just above a pool of liquid nitrogen
experiments.description: The equipment-light alternative in the USDA ARS National Animal Germplasm Program bull-semen protocol (no programmable freezer): 0.5 mL straws on a rack are held in static liquid-nitrogen vapour 4.5 cm above the liquid surface for 10 min and then plunged into the liquid nitrogen, where they are stored at liquid-nitrogen temperature until thawing at 37 °C for insemination.

requirements.rationale: Freezing happens in the vapour 4.5 cm above a liquid-nitrogen pool and the straws are then plunged into the liquid nitrogen, so the container must hold liquid nitrogen.

experiments.name: Slow freezing of bovine (and ovine/caprine) preimplantation embryos in ethylene glycol in 0.25 mL straws: seeding at -6 °C, 0.5 °C/min to -34 °C, plunge into liquid nitrogen (-196 °C) for direct transfer
experiments.plain_name: Slow-freeze cattle embryos in straws so they can later be transferred into surrogate cows
experiments.description: Livestock embryo-transfer practice described by Youngs (JoVE 2011): embryos equilibrated in 1.4-1.5 M ethylene glycol or glycerol are loaded individually into 0.25 mL straws, placed in a controlled-rate freezer at -6 °C, seeded with liquid-nitrogen-cooled tongs, held 10 min, cooled at 0.5 °C/min to -34 °C, held 10 min and plunged into liquid nitrogen (-196 °C) for storage in dewar canisters; ethylene-glycol embryos can be transferred directly after thawing.

requirements.rationale: The freezer chamber must hold the seeding temperature -6 °C (267.15 K) and cool to the plunge temperature -34 °C (239.15 K).

requirements.rationale: The controlled cooling rate after seeding is 0.5 °C/min (500 mK/min).

experiments.name: Long-term (base-collection) storage of dried orthodox crop seed at -18 ± 3 °C and 15 ± 3% RH in sealed airtight containers (FAO Genebank Standard 4.2.3)
experiments.plain_name: Keep a seed bank's master copies of crop seeds in a minus-18 freezer for decades
experiments.description: Genebanks conserve the most-original samples and safety duplicates of orthodox crop seed (maize, wheat, rice, etc.) after drying to equilibrium at 5-20 °C and 10-25% RH, sealing in airtight containers and storing at -18 ± 3 °C. The same -18 °C regime is used at the Svalbard Global Seed Vault (artificial cooling keeps a constant -18 C) and for USDA ARS original (base) seed collections.

requirements.rationale: Base collections are stored at a set point of -18 °C (255.15 K).
requirements.document_title: FAO (2014). Genebank Standards for Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture. Rome, FAO (I3704E)
requirements.location: Section 4.2 'Standards for drying and storage', Standard 4.2.3, printed page 24 (PDF page 37)
requirements.quote: Most-original-samples and safety duplicate samples should be stored under long-term conditions (base collections) at a temperature of –18 ± 3 °C and relative humidity of 15 ± 3 percent.

requirements.rationale: The standard asks for storage within ±3 °C of the set temperature; optional because it is phrased as best effort with limited excursions allowed.
requirements.document_title: FAO (2014). Genebank Standards for Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture. Rome, FAO (I3704E)
requirements.quote: For long-term stored seeds, all attempts should be made to maintain storage temperatures within ±3 °C of the set temperature

requirements.rationale: Standard 4.2.3 also gives 15 ± 3% storage RH; optional because Standard 4.2.2 seals the seed in airtight containers and USDA base collections at -18 °C do not control RH.

experiments.name: Dormant-bud cryopreservation of Malus and Pyrus germplasm: 35 mm single-bud stem sections dehydrated to 30% moisture, cooled at 1 °C/h to -30 °C in a Kryo 360-3.3, held 24 h, stored in LN2 vapour
experiments.plain_name: Back up apple and pear tree varieties by slowly freezing their winter buds
experiments.description: Fruit Genebank Dresden-Pillnitz (JKI) duplicate-collection method: winter-dormant budwood is cut into 35 mm single-bud sections, dehydrated to 30% moisture at -5 °C, placed in 4.5 mL cryovials, cooled at 1 °C/h to -30 °C in a controlled-rate freezer, held at -30 °C for 24 h, transferred to the vapour phase over liquid nitrogen, and later rewarmed at +4 °C for 24 h before grafting.

requirements.rationale: The controlled-rate freezer must reach and hold -30 °C (243.15 K) for 24 h.
requirements.document_title: Hoefer M, Flachowsky H (2023). Cryopreservation of Malus and Pyrus Wild Species in the 'Fruit Genebank' in Dresden-Pillnitz, Germany. Biology 12(2):200. doi:10.3390/biology12020200

experiments.name: Droplet vitrification of sweet potato axillary meristems (20 min LS, 30 min PVS2 on ice, aluminium foil strip plunged into liquid nitrogen, held in 2 mL cryotubes of LN)
experiments.plain_name: Preserve sweet potato varieties by flash-freezing tiny shoot tips on foil strips
experiments.description: Clonal-crop genebank method (KU Leuven / Bioversity International): 1 mm3 axillary meristems are loaded for 20 min, dehydrated 30 min in PVS2 in an ice bath, placed in droplets on a 4 x 15 mm aluminium foil strip, plunged into liquid nitrogen and kept for at least 30 min in a 2 mL cryotube filled with liquid nitrogen before rewarming in recovery solution at room temperature; cryopreservation of shoot tips in LN at -196 °C is the FAO-recognised long-term route for vegetatively propagated food crops.

requirements.rationale: The foil strip is plunged into liquid nitrogen and the meristems are held in a cryotube filled with liquid nitrogen.
requirements.document_title: Wilms H, Fanega Sleziak N, Van der Auweraer M, et al., Panis B (2020). Development of a fast and user-friendly cryopreservation protocol for sweet potato genetic resources. Scientific Reports 10:14674. doi:10.1038/s41598-020-70869-3

requirements.rationale: Cryopreserved plant shoot tips are held at the liquid-nitrogen temperature, -196 °C (77.15 K).

experiments.name: Liquid-nitrogen quick freezing of 'Northcountry' blueberries at -80, -100 and -120 °C to below Tg' (-52.55 °C), compared with a -80 °C ultra-low freezer
experiments.plain_name: Flash-freeze blueberries in liquid nitrogen to keep them firm and juicy
experiments.description: Blueberries were frozen to their glass-transition end point (Tg' = -52.55 °C) either in an ultra-low temperature freezer at -80 °C or by direct immersion in liquid nitrogen at set points of -80, -100 and -120 °C; LN-120 °C gave the least quality loss (juice loss, hardness, anthocyanin, membrane integrity, microstructure).

requirements.rationale: The best-performing treatment, LN-120 °C, needs the freezing space at -120 °C (153.15 K).
requirements.document_title: Huang B, Li Y, Hu Z (2024). Effect of Glassy State and Liquid Nitrogen Quick Freezing on the Quality Characteristics of Blueberries. Food Science (Shipin Kexue) 45(6):225-232. doi:10.7506/spkx1002-6630-20230629-236
requirements.quote: or at −80, −100 or −120 ℃ by direct immersion in liquid nitrogen (LN−80 ℃, LN−100 ℃, and LN−120 ℃, respectively).

requirements.rationale: Freezing is done by direct immersion in liquid nitrogen.

experiments.name: Cryogenic grinding of cumin seed (genotypes GC 4 and RZ 209) with liquid-nitrogen pre-cooling to a -30 °C set point in a Fine Impact Mill 100UPZ, 50-100 um powder
experiments.plain_name: Grind cumin seeds into spice powder while liquid nitrogen keeps their aroma in
experiments.description: ICAR-National Research Centre on Seed Spices: cumin seed is chilled by liquid nitrogen sprayed and blended directly onto it until it reaches a -30 °C set point, then ground in a pin (impact) mill to 50-100 um; cryo-grinding raised volatile-oil recovery by 33.9-43.5% over a conventional mixer grinder.

requirements.rationale: The procedure is mechanical comminution with cryogenic cooling; a machine without a grinding function cannot perform it.
requirements.document_title: Sharma LK, Agarwal D, Rathore SS, Malhotra SK, Saxena SN (2016). Effect of cryogenic grinding on volatile and fatty oil constituents of cumin (Cuminum cyminum L.) genotypes. Journal of Food Science and Technology 53(6):2827-2834. doi:10.1007/s13197-016-2258-0
requirements.quote: Cryogenic grinding of seeds was done using a cryogenic grinder (Spectra cryogenics, India) model Fine Impact Mill 100UPZ

requirements.rationale: The seed is cooled to a predetermined set point of -30 °C (243.15 K) before milling.

experiments.name: Long-term ultra-low-temperature frozen storage of tuna meat at -45 °C or lower to prevent metmyoglobin (browning) formation
experiments.plain_name: Store sashimi tuna deep-frozen cold enough that its red colour does not turn brown
experiments.description: Nakazawa et al. (Int. J. Refrigeration 2020) stored low-pH and high-pH tuna meat at a range of frozen-storage temperatures over long periods: metMb% rose in low-pH meat held warmer than -40 °C, while no increase occurred at -45 °C or lower regardless of pH, supporting ultra-low-temperature storage of tuna.

requirements.rationale: Colour stability (no metMb increase) needs storage at -45 °C (228.15 K) or colder; either a documented range reaching that low or a documented lowest temperature settles it.
requirements.document_title: Nakazawa N, Wada R, Fukushima H, Tanaka R, Kono S, Okazaki E (2020). Effect of long-term storage, ultra-low temperature, and freshness on the quality characteristics of frozen tuna meat. International Journal of Refrigeration 112:270-280. doi:10.1016/j.ijrefrig.2019.12.012 (IIR FRIDOC abstract record)
requirements.quote: An increase in the metMb% was not observed in meat stored at −45 °C or lower, irrespective of the pH.

requirements.rationale: Storage warmer than -40 °C (233.15 K) increased metMb in low-pH meat; optional because the -45 °C requirement already covers it.
requirements.document_title: Nakazawa N, Wada R, Fukushima H, Tanaka R, Kono S, Okazaki E (2020). requirements.quote: The increase in metMb% was higher in the Low-pH samples stored at temperatures higher than −40 °C.
